override.reason: Stakeholder override, 2026-10-11: the review blocked on 20 MED findings. Four were real errors and are corrected in the definition (SQL already indexed as a whole document; what reindexFile removes; the local model named as the cheap tier; the file-event check's location). Sixteen were checks the reviewer could not finish because its searches stop at 50 matches; fourteen were verified by hand and two (the daemon shutdown path, the migration on open) are left for the design stage. The corrections were made after the review and were not re-reviewed. Details are in the definition's feedback record.

summary.prose: Answers about a codebase are only as good as the index behind them. This Epic makes the index complete (no relationship is lost, nothing is left out that the repository did not ask to leave out, and a repository that is incomplete says so), consistent (a file's refresh either happens in full or not at all, and the daemon stays healthy while it works), and richer (each relationship says how it was found, related code is grouped into subsystems with summaries, Rust, C#, C and C++ are read, SQL is read in its structure where today it is stored as one whole document, and relationships between documents are recorded). It brings five filed issues under one design, so the changes they share are made once.

body.problem: The code index cannot be trusted to be complete or consistent, and it records less than it could. Relationships between files are lost while a repository is indexed and are never restored, yet the repository reports itself ready and answers are returned as plain facts with nothing to say they may be partial [[c4]]. A single file's refresh is a series of separate removals and writes, so an error or a crash part-way leaves the file with no entities, or with entities and no relationships [[c2]]. Reading the entities of one file or one repository passes over every stored row [[c5]], the daemon's store can be broken under it by another process, after which it cannot be stopped [[c12]], and the code that reads the index's state reports a scope the index does not hold as the largest size and lets a failed read of the last-indexed time escape as an unexplained error [[c13]] [[c14]]. What the index leaves out is decided twice, by two rules that disagree: a full walk follows the repository's own ignore files, and then a separate list of bare names is applied to every part of every path, so a source directory that the repository does not ignore can be hidden, a rule meant for the top level applies at every depth, later edits to the ignore files never reach the list, and a file event is checked against the list alone [[c16]] [[c17]] [[c18]]. Beyond these defects, a stored relationship carries no record of how it was established [[c1]], the index holds no grouping of related code into subsystems, and it reads the structure of only six programming languages (TypeScript with JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, Scala and Kotlin), stores an SQL file only as one whole document, and records no relationships between documents. These have been found and filed one at a time, with overlapping changes to the same store and the same refresh path, and no single statement of what a correct index is.

nonGoals.text: Replacing LMDB or LanceDB, or adopting Graphify as a dependency or as the index.
nonGoals.rationale: The comparison found additions to the ingestion and context layers; none requires a different store.
The project rule is a typed traversal API only.

nonGoals.text: Calling a cloud model service directly from the daemon.
nonGoals.rationale: Model access beyond the local provider goes through the installed CLI providers only.

nonGoals.text: Sources of exclusion rules other than git's own ignore sources.
nonGoals.rationale: The stakeholder limited the filter to those sources for now; the filter leaves room for other sources later but this Epic delivers none.

nonGoals.text: Changing an ignore file that already exists in a repository.
nonGoals.rationale: The repository's own file is the user's statement of what to leave out; the daemon only creates one where none exists at the root.

nonGoals.text: The analyzer's own planning and report defects (Epic b9d5c5c40df5a574).
nonGoals.rationale: That Epic owns the analyzer above the index; this Epic takes only the defects in how the index's state is read.

nonGoals.text: New entity and relation kinds for external services (Epic 914cbf5ea9026b92).
nonGoals.rationale: Owned by that Epic; this Epic must not renumber the kinds it added.

nonGoals.text: Languages beyond Rust, C#, SQL, C and C++, and extraction from images, audio or video.
nonGoals.rationale: The stakeholder named these languages for now; the rest is outside the ask.

nonGoals.text: Keeping the embedding model loaded during indexing.
nonGoals.rationale: Checked on current code: every embedding call already asks for the model to stay loaded, so there is nothing to change.

assumptions.text: Fixing the lost relationships first changes the graph that grouping and summaries are computed from, so enrichment built before it would be built on a wrong graph.

The unused whole-file replacement in the store is a sound base for an all-or-nothing refresh. It replaces a file's entities and removes the relationships of the entities it replaces, in one transaction; it does not write the file's new relationships and does not touch the unresolved queue, so it must be extended to both.
The store's edge rows can carry a value without changing their keys, so evidence can be added to existing stores by a migration.
The local model can propose a usable ignore file for a project and usable subsystem summaries; where it cannot, a plain fallback is acceptable.
The mid-tier model can reach 95% right and 60% found on document relationships; this is not known until it is measured.
The mid-tier model is reached through a CLI provider on the user's own session, so extracting document relationships spends that session's quota.

constraints.text: Accuracy is chosen over cost: a slower index that is complete is preferred to a fast one that loses relationships.
Only the daemon opens the stores; every new read or write is reached through the daemon.
No direct cloud REST calls: a model is reached through the local provider or through the installed CLI providers.
Calls that reach a model provider are made one after another, never in parallel.
The store has a schema version; a change to what is stored comes with a migration applied when the daemon opens the store, without a user re-index.
Entity and relation kinds are stored as fixed byte values; existing values are never renumbered.
The Stories that make the index complete and consistent are delivered before the Stories that enrich it.
Each absorbed issue keeps its identity: its Story names it, and the issue is marked as consolidated into this Epic rather than closed unfixed.

The proposal of an ignore file and the subsystem summaries use the local model, meaning the tier named cheap, which the local Ollama provider serves by default; the extraction of document relationships uses the mid-tier model; embeddings stay local.
Model-proposed document relationships are used only when at least 95% of those proposed are right and at least 60% of the real ones are found, measured on at least 100 hand-checked links.

The exclusion rule comes from git's own ignore sources only: the repository's .gitignore files, including those in subdirectories, each applying to its own directory and below, the clone's exclude file and the user's global ignore file. A file that git tracks is indexed even when a rule matches it. Two built-in exclusions stand beside git's sources and apply at every place that selects files: generated or minified files, and the daemon's own .insrc directory.

stories.title: No relationship between indexed files is lost, and a damaged index can be repaired (ISSUE-12f70133)
stories.userValue: Someone asking what calls or imports a piece of code gets every caller and importer the source contains, and a repository that cannot give that says so instead of answering with a partial count.

localConstraints.text: This Story absorbs ISSUE-12f70133491114c9 in full, including its reproduction figures as the acceptance measure, except the figure for pickScope, a function since removed from the source.

functionalRequirements.statement: A relationship whose target has not been indexed yet is kept and completed once the target exists.

A reindex removes everything the index holds for the repository, in the graph store and in the vector store, and builds it again from every file; it is the one command for this, and there is no separate repair.
A call that reaches a function through a re-exporting file is linked to that function.
A repository whose graph is known to be incomplete does not report itself as fully ready, and a relationship that cannot be written is surfaced rather than skipped silently.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository in which a file that sorts earlier imports and calls into a file that sorts later
acceptanceCriteria.when: the repository is indexed in full for the first time
acceptanceCriteria.then: the import and the call are both stored, and asking for the callers of the later file's function returns the earlier file's call site

acceptanceCriteria.given: this repository with an index that has already lost cross-file relationships
acceptanceCriteria.when: a reindex of the repository is requested, without removing it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the callers of runGrepSearch are 4, as the issue's reproduction expects, and the callers of one function that this repository reaches only through a re-exporting file, named in the Story's design with its count from a text search, match that count

acceptanceCriteria.given: a function that is reached only through a file that re-exports it
acceptanceCriteria.when: the callers of that function are requested
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call sites that go through the re-exporting file are returned

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository in which some relationships could not be written or remain unresolved after indexing
acceptanceCriteria.when: the repository's status is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: a completeness field shown wherever the status is shown says the graph is incomplete and gives the count, so the repository does not read as fully ready

stories.title: Refreshing one file happens in full or not at all
stories.userValue: A file being re-indexed never disappears from answers, and a failure or a crash during a refresh leaves the file as it was before, not half-written.

localConstraints.text: The store already holds a whole-file replacement that nothing calls; the refresh builds on it rather than adding a second one.

functionalRequirements.statement: The removal of a file's old entities, relationships and pending relationships and the writing of its new ones take effect together in the graph store.
A refresh that fails before it completes leaves the file's previous entities and relationships readable.
A refresh whose vectors were not written after the graph store was updated is detected and completed without the user asking.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an indexed file and a refresh of it that fails after its content is parsed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the file's entities and relationships are read afterwards
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are the ones stored before the refresh began

acceptanceCriteria.given: an indexed file whose refresh is in progress
acceptanceCriteria.when: another request reads the file's entities during the refresh
acceptanceCriteria.then: it sees either the complete old set or the complete new set, never an empty or partial set

acceptanceCriteria.given: a refresh that updated the graph store but whose vector write failed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon next starts or the repository is next checked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the missing vectors are found and written, and the repository is not reported as fully ready until they are

acceptanceCriteria.given: a file deleted from disk
acceptanceCriteria.when: the deletion is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: its entities, relationships and pending relationships are removed together

stories.title: Reading one file's or one repository's entities does not pass over the whole store (ISSUE-61045de9)
stories.userValue: Requests about one file or one repository stay fast as more repositories are indexed, because their cost follows what they return.

localConstraints.text: This Story absorbs ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0 in full; the two reads return what they return today and their callers do not change.

functionalRequirements.statement: The entities of one file, and of one repository, are read without passing over the rows of other files and other repositories.
Whether a repository holds any stored entity is answered without building the repository's entities.
A store already on disk gains this when the daemon opens it, without the user re-indexing.

acceptanceCriteria.given: two indexed repositories, one much larger than the other
acceptanceCriteria.when: the entities of one file of the smaller repository are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the read examines only that file's rows, and returns the same entities as before

acceptanceCriteria.given: a store written before this change
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon opens it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the store is brought to the new form once, the reads work without a re-index, and a second open does no further work

acceptanceCriteria.given: entities written, replaced and deleted for a file
acceptanceCriteria.when: the file's entities are read after each change
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result matches a full scan of the store every time

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with stored entities and one with none
acceptanceCriteria.when: the scope check asks whether each holds any entity
acceptanceCriteria.then: it answers yes and no without reading the repository's entities

stories.title: The daemon's store is not broken by another process, and the daemon always stops (ISSUE-0d577569)
stories.userValue: The daemon keeps running through long indexing and many requests, and when something does go wrong in the store it can still be stopped and restarted normally.

localConstraints.text: This Story absorbs ISSUE-0d577569 in full; that issue is already approved and its statement of the symptoms stands. Its cause, which the issue records as not established, was reproduced on 2026-10-11: not the system's semaphore limit, which the library's message names, but the loss of the daemon's own file lock on the store's lock file, after which another process that opens and closes the store removes the store's semaphores.

functionalRequirements.statement: No other process's opening or closing of a store takes the daemon's locks away: the live store is opened by the daemon alone.
When a store operation fails, the daemon still stops when asked.
A store failure of this kind is reported with its cause where the user looks for daemon status.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a running daemon, and another process that tries to open the live store
acceptanceCriteria.when: that process opens and closes a store and the daemon then writes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the other process is refused the live store, and the daemon's write succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.given: a daemon in which a store operation has failed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon is asked to stop
acceptanceCriteria.then: it stops within its normal stop time and can be started again without manual clean-up

acceptanceCriteria.given: a store operation that fails because the store's locks were taken away
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon's status is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the failure and its true cause are stated, not the library's message about a system limit

stories.title: Reads of the index's state give a named, truthful answer (ISSUE-a6940f8a, ISSUE-e2bcadd9)
stories.userValue: A request about code the index does not hold is refused for that reason, and never looks like a very large request or an unexplained internal error, and a request made while the repository is being indexed is told so instead of being answered from a half-built index.

localConstraints.text: This Story absorbs ISSUE-a6940f8a and all four defects of ISSUE-e2bcadd9; a refused request keeps the code and message it has today.

functionalRequirements.statement: A request whose scope will be refused is refused before it is announced with a size, or its announcement makes plain that its size could not be counted.
A failure to read a repository's last-indexed time, or a failure inside a lookup, is one of the named causes of not proceeding.
The remaining defects recorded in ISSUE-e2bcadd9 are closed as that issue states them.

While a repository is being indexed or reindexed, a search or analyze request about it is refused with a named error that states the indexing state; no partial answer is returned. Only that repository is offline: requests about other repositories are answered as usual.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a request whose scope the index does not hold
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request is run
acceptanceCriteria.then: no event announces it as the largest size, and it is refused with the same code and message as today

acceptanceCriteria.given: a read of a repository's last-indexed time that throws
acceptanceCriteria.when: a context is being built for a request
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request ends with a named cause and its own error code, not an internal error

acceptanceCriteria.given: each of the four reproductions in ISSUE-e2bcadd9
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is run
acceptanceCriteria.then: the expected result that issue states is observed

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository whose index or reindex is in progress, or ended in an error before it completed
acceptanceCriteria.when: a search request or an analyze request about that repository is made
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request is refused with a named error and its own code that says the repository is being indexed and how far the run has got, and no partial result is returned

stories.title: One rule decides what the index leaves out, taken from the repository's ignore files
stories.userValue: The index holds exactly the files the repository does not ask to leave out: no source directory goes missing because of its name, an edit to an ignore file takes effect, and a repository that had no ignore file gets a sensible one when it is added.

localConstraints.text: The separate list of bare names stops deciding what is left out; a repository that carries such a list from an earlier registration is not left with two rules.
A failure of the model call that proposes an ignore file does not fail the adding of the repository; a plain ignore file is written instead and the fallback is stated.
The filter is built so that a source of rules other than ignore files can be added later; this Story adds none.

functionalRequirements.statement: A file is left out of the index when, and only when, git's ignore sources leave it out and git does not track it, with two named exceptions that are left out everywhere: a generated or minified file, and anything in the daemon's own .insrc directory.
Ignore files in subdirectories are honoured, each for its own directory and below.
A full walk, a single file event and the watcher apply the same rule.
A change to an ignore file takes effect without the repository being removed and added again: newly ignored files leave the index and newly included files enter it.
A repository added with no ignore file at its root is given one whose entries fit the project, proposed by a model that has looked at the repository.
An ignore file that already exists is never changed.
A folder that is not under version control is filtered by the same ignore files.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository whose ignore file leaves out a top-level directory by an anchored rule, and which has a source directory of the same name deeper in its tree
acceptanceCriteria.when: the repository is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the deeper directory's files are indexed and the top-level one's are not

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with a tracked source directory whose name is on today's built-in list of names but is not left out by any ignore file
acceptanceCriteria.when: the repository is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: that directory's files are indexed

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with an ignore file in a subdirectory that leaves out files under it
acceptanceCriteria.when: the repository is indexed and when one of those files is later changed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the files are left out both times, and files of the same name elsewhere in the tree are indexed

acceptanceCriteria.given: a file left out by a pattern rule in an ignore file
acceptanceCriteria.when: a change to that file arrives as a single file event
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file is not indexed

acceptanceCriteria.given: an indexed repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: a rule is added to one of its ignore files and another is removed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the files the new rule covers leave the index and the files the removed rule covered enter it, without re-adding the repository

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with no ignore file at its root
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is added
acceptanceCriteria.then: an ignore file is created at its root with entries that fit the project's languages and tools, proposed by the local model, before the first index runs

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with no ignore file at its root and a model call that fails
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is added
acceptanceCriteria.then: the repository is still added, a plain ignore file is written, and the result says the fallback was used

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository that already has an ignore file at its root
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is added or indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file is byte-for-byte unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.given: a folder that is not under version control and has ignore files at its root and in a subdirectory
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the files its ignore files leave out are left out, as untracked files would be under version control

stories.title: Every stored relationship says how it was established
stories.userValue: A reader of an answer can tell a relationship read straight from the source from one the indexer inferred or chose among candidates, and weigh it accordingly.

localConstraints.text: Relationships stored before this change are not presented as if their origin were known.

functionalRequirements.statement: Each stored relationship records whether it was read directly from the source, inferred by resolution, or chosen among several candidates.
The record is returned with the relationship wherever relationships are read.
A relationship stored before this change reads as of unknown origin until its file is next refreshed.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a file with a call to a function in the same file and a call resolved across files
acceptanceCriteria.when: the file is indexed and its relationships are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first is marked as read from the source and the second as inferred

acceptanceCriteria.given: a call that matches several candidate targets
acceptanceCriteria.when: the relationship is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is kept as pending with its candidates and reported as ambiguous, no target is guessed, and the value 'chosen among candidates' is reserved for a choosing rule that this Epic does not add

acceptanceCriteria.given: a store written before this change
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon opens it and a relationship is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the relationship is returned and marked as of unknown origin, with no re-index required

acceptanceCriteria.given: an analyzer answer that lists callers
acceptanceCriteria.when: some of the listed callers rest on inferred or chosen relationships
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answer says which

stories.title: The index groups related code into subsystems and the analyzer's context summarises them
stories.userValue: A question about an area of the code comes back with the subsystem it belongs to, what that subsystem does and what it connects to, not only a list of files.

localConstraints.text: Groups are computed from the stored graph only after it is complete; a repository whose graph is incomplete has no groups presented as settled.

functionalRequirements.statement: Each indexed repository's code is grouped into subsystems from its stored relationships.
Each subsystem has a summary and a list of its connections to other subsystems.
The analyzer's context for a request includes the summaries of the subsystems the request touches.
Grouping is repeatable: the same graph gives the same groups.
Subsystem summaries are written by the local model.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a fully indexed repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: its subsystems are requested through the daemon
acceptanceCriteria.then: every code entity belongs to exactly one subsystem and each subsystem lists its connections to the others

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same stored graph
acceptanceCriteria.when: grouping is run twice
acceptanceCriteria.then: the groups are the same

acceptanceCriteria.given: a request about one module
acceptanceCriteria.when: the analyzer builds its context
acceptanceCriteria.then: the context names the subsystem the module belongs to, its summary and its connections, each traceable to stored entities

acceptanceCriteria.given: subsystem summaries being written
acceptanceCriteria.when: the model calls are made
acceptanceCriteria.then: they go to the local model, one at a time

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository whose graph is reported incomplete
acceptanceCriteria.when: its subsystems are requested
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answer says the groups rest on an incomplete graph

stories.title: The index reads Rust, C#, SQL, C and C++
stories.userValue: Repositories written in Rust, C#, SQL, C or C++ become answerable, with the same kinds of entities and relationships as the languages read today.

localConstraints.text: The languages are those the stakeholder named: Rust, C#, SQL, C and C++. Each can be delivered and checked on its own.

functionalRequirements.statement: Files in Rust, C#, C and C++ produce entities and relationships of the same kinds as the languages read today.
SQL files produce entities for the objects they define and relationships for the objects they refer to, where today an SQL file is stored as one whole document.
A language whose reader cannot be loaded on a machine is skipped with a stated reason, and the other languages are unaffected.
The languages the index reads are listed where the user can see them.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with files in Rust, C#, C and C++
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: for each of those languages its functions, types and files are stored as entities and its imports or includes and its calls as relationships

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with SQL files that define tables and views and refer to other tables
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: each defined object is stored as an entity and each reference to another object as a relationship

acceptanceCriteria.given: a machine on which the reader for one of the added languages cannot be loaded
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon starts and indexes a mixed repository
acceptanceCriteria.then: that language's files are skipped with a stated reason and every other language is indexed

acceptanceCriteria.given: the set of languages the index reads
acceptanceCriteria.when: a user asks for it through the daemon
acceptanceCriteria.then: Rust, C#, SQL, C and C++ are listed with the six read today

stories.title: The index records relationships between documents, admitted only at a measured quality
stories.userValue: A question about a design or a rule finds the documents that bear on it through what they say about each other, and the reader can see which links a model proposed.

localConstraints.text: If the measured quality does not meet the bar the capability stays off and the measured figures are recorded.
Model extraction spends the user's CLI session quota, so it runs only for documents that are new or changed, and indexing completes without it when no CLI provider is available.

functionalRequirements.statement: Relationships between documents, and between a document and the code it describes, are stored.
A relationship a model proposed is marked as such, apart from one read directly from a link or a reference in the text.
Model-proposed relationships are extracted by the mid-tier model.
Model-proposed relationships are used only when at least 95% of those proposed are right and at least 60% of the real ones are found, on at least 100 hand-checked links.
Only new or changed documents are sent to the model.

acceptanceCriteria.given: two documents where one links to or names the other
acceptanceCriteria.when: they are indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the relationship is stored and marked as read from the source, with no model call

acceptanceCriteria.given: a hand-checked set of at least 100 document relationships for this repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: the mid-tier model's proposals are compared with it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the share that are right and the share that are found are recorded, and the capability is on only if the first is at least 95% and the second at least 60%

acceptanceCriteria.given: model-proposed relationships that are stored
acceptanceCriteria.when: they are read or used in an answer
acceptanceCriteria.then: each is marked as proposed by a model

acceptanceCriteria.given: documents being examined by a model
acceptanceCriteria.when: the indexing run makes its model calls
acceptanceCriteria.then: the calls go to the mid-tier model through a CLI provider, one at a time

acceptanceCriteria.given: an indexed repository in which one document has changed
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is indexed again
acceptanceCriteria.then: only that document is sent to the model

acceptanceCriteria.given: a machine with no CLI provider signed in
acceptanceCriteria.when: a repository is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: indexing completes, relationships read from the source are stored, and the status says model-proposed document relationships were not extracted and why

stories.title: The step tools run inside the daemon, and the MCP server opens no store
stories.userValue: An analysis, a workflow step, a review or a triage asked for from a client session is carried out by the daemon, so no client session's process ever holds the live store open, and a run in progress is not lost when the session's MCP server process restarts.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a client session and a running daemon
acceptanceCriteria.when: an analyze step, a workflow step, a build step, a review step, a code-review step or a triage step is called from the session
acceptanceCriteria.then: the step's lookups and its reads and writes of the store happen in the daemon, the result returned to the session is the same as before, and the MCP server's process holds no descriptor on the live store

acceptanceCriteria.given: a multi-turn run that has received its first reply
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session's MCP server process exits and a new one starts before the next turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the next turn is accepted with the state token from the first reply and the run continues

acceptanceCriteria.given: a client session and no running daemon, or a daemon that does not know the request
acceptanceCriteria.when: a step tool is called
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call returns a named error that says the daemon is not reachable or is too old, and nothing is read from the store by the MCP server's process

acceptanceCriteria.given: the source tree after this change
acceptanceCriteria.when: the files under the MCP server's directory and everything they import outside the daemon's request client are scanned
acceptanceCriteria.then: none of them opens the graph store or the vector store

acceptanceCriteria.given: a step that needs the client's own model to answer a prompt
acceptanceCriteria.when: the daemon returns that prompt
acceptanceCriteria.then: the prompt, the schema and the state token reach the client unchanged, and the reasoning still happens in the session, as it does today

acceptanceCriteria.given: the temporary allowance that Story s4 gives the MCP server's process to open the live store (the permitted-reader declaration and its one call)
acceptanceCriteria.when: this Story is delivered
acceptanceCriteria.then: the declaration and its call are deleted from the source, the MCP server's process is refused the live store like any other process that is not the daemon, and a test fails if the declaration is found anywhere in the source

acceptanceCriteria.given: a process that is not the daemon (a test, a script, a client session's MCP server or any tool)
acceptanceCriteria.when: it asks to open the live vector store (the ~/.insrc/lance directory, reached directly, by a relative path or through a symbolic link)
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused with a named error before the directory is created or connected, while a temporary path set for a test opens as before, so only the daemon ever opens the live vector store, as Story s4 made true of the graph store

localConstraints.text: Removing the temporary allowance is part of this Story and not optional: by the stakeholder's decision of 2026-10-11 the allowance exists only until this Story lands, and Story s4's first acceptance criterion is met in full only when it is gone.

functionalRequirements.statement: The temporary allowance for the MCP server's process to open the live store is removed with this Story.

stories.title: Every supported parser records the calls its code makes, and calls resolve within a package
stories.userValue: Someone asking what calls a function, or a code review asking which tests reach a change, gets the true answer in every supported language, not only in TypeScript: Python and Go record calls at all, calls outside methods (class bodies, initializers, scripts) are recorded in every parser, JVM callee names match what resolution looks up, and calls between files of one package resolve without an import.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a Python test function calling a function imported from another module, and a Go TestX calling a function in another file of the same package
acceptanceCriteria.when: the repository is indexed and the callers of the called function are requested
acceptanceCriteria.then: each test is returned as a caller, and the code-review grounding lists the test file in the function's testsReaching

acceptanceCriteria.given: a ScalaTest class-body test("x") { ... }, a Kotest FunSpec({ test("x") { ... } }) lambda, a Kotlin init block, a Java initializer block, a field or property initializer and a Python class-body statement, each calling a function
acceptanceCriteria.when: the file is indexed
acceptanceCriteria.then: each call is a CALLS relation from the nearest enclosing entity (the class, variable or property), never dropped

acceptanceCriteria.given: a Java qualified call obj.method() and a Scala receiver call x.method(s), where method is defined on a class in the repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: the cross-file pass runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call resolves to that method, or is reported ambiguous with its candidates; it is not left unresolved

acceptanceCriteria.given: a JUnit test under src/test/java/com/x calling a class in src/main/java/com/x, and a Kotlin test calling a function in another file of its package
acceptanceCriteria.when: the cross-file pass runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: both calls resolve without an import

stories.title: Settling file changes does work proportional to the changed files, never a scan of the repository or the store
stories.userValue: After an edit, a branch switch or a merge, the graph catches up in time proportional to what changed: a burst of file events no longer costs one whole-repository resolve per file, and reading one file's or one repository's entities no longer passes over every other repository's rows. The results are the same as a full index gives.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository whose index is complete, and one file in it that changes
acceptanceCriteria.when: the settle pass for that file event runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the entity rows, pending rows and edges it reads are those the changed file defines, imports, exports or awaits, and their number does not grow with the size of the repository or of the store

acceptanceCriteria.given: a burst of file events touching N files of a repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: their settle work runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the work done grows with N and with what those files touch, not with N times the repository

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same file changes settled event by event, and the same files indexed by a full index
acceptanceCriteria.when: the edges and pending-row classes of those files are compared
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are identical

acceptanceCriteria.given: a store holding several repositories
acceptanceCriteria.when: the entities of one file, or of one repository, are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: no row of another file or another repository is read, and the result is what it is today

requirements.statement: Every relationship the indexer establishes between two indexed entities is stored, whatever order the files were indexed in.
requirements.rationale: ISSUE-12f70133: edges to not-yet-stored targets are dropped.

requirements.statement: An index that already lost relationships can be repaired without the user deleting and re-adding the repository.
requirements.rationale: A reindex skips unchanged files today.

requirements.statement: A repository whose graph is known to be incomplete does not report itself as fully ready, and a relationship that cannot be written is surfaced.
requirements.rationale: Silent partial answers are the accuracy failure.

requirements.statement: The refresh of one file is all-or-nothing in the graph store, and a refresh interrupted before its vectors are written is detected and completed.
The entities of one file, and of one repository, are read at a cost that grows with what is returned, and an existing store gains this without a user re-index.
The daemon's store is not broken by another process, and the daemon always stops when asked, a failed store included.
A request whose scope the index does not hold is refused without first being announced as the largest size, and every failure to read the index's state is a named cause.
What the index leaves out is decided by one rule, taken from the repository's ignore files at every level of its tree, and applied the same way to a full walk and to a single file event.
A repository added without an ignore file at its root is given one, with entries that fit the project.
Every stored relationship records how it was established: read directly from the source, inferred by resolution, or chosen among several candidates.
The index groups related code into subsystems, and the analyzer's context includes a summary of each relevant subsystem and the connections between subsystems.
The index reads the structure of Rust, C#, SQL, C and C++ files in addition to today's six languages; an SQL file is stored today only as one whole document.
The index records relationships between documents; a relationship a model proposed is marked as such and is used only when measured quality meets the stated bar.
A relationship whose target has not been indexed yet is kept and completed once the target exists.

A reindex removes everything the index holds for the repository, in the graph store and in the vector store, and builds it again from every file; it is the one command for this, and there is no separate repair.
A call that reaches a function through a re-exporting file is linked to that function.
A repository whose graph is known to be incomplete does not report itself as fully ready, and a relationship that cannot be written is surfaced rather than skipped silently.
The removal of a file's old entities, relationships and pending relationships and the writing of its new ones take effect together in the graph store.
A refresh that fails before it completes leaves the file's previous entities and relationships readable.
A refresh whose vectors were not written after the graph store was updated is detected and completed without the user asking.
The entities of one file, and of one repository, are read without passing over the rows of other files and other repositories.
Whether a repository holds any stored entity is answered without building the repository's entities.
A store already on disk gains this when the daemon opens it, without the user re-indexing.
No other process's opening or closing of a store takes the daemon's locks away: the live store is opened by the daemon alone.
When a store operation fails, the daemon still stops when asked.
A store failure of this kind is reported with its cause where the user looks for daemon status.
A request whose scope will be refused is refused before it is announced with a size, or its announcement makes plain that its size could not be counted.
A failure to read a repository's last-indexed time, or a failure inside a lookup, is one of the named causes of not proceeding.
The remaining defects recorded in ISSUE-e2bcadd9 are closed as that issue states them.

While a repository is being indexed or reindexed, a search or analyze request about it is refused with a named error that states the indexing state; no partial answer is returned. Only that repository is offline: requests about other repositories are answered as usual.

A file is left out of the index when, and only when, git's ignore sources leave it out and git does not track it, with two named exceptions that are left out everywhere: a generated or minified file, and anything in the daemon's own .insrc directory.
Ignore files in subdirectories are honoured, each for its own directory and below.
A full walk, a single file event and the watcher apply the same rule.
A change to an ignore file takes effect without the repository being removed and added again: newly ignored files leave the index and newly included files enter it.
A repository added with no ignore file at its root is given one whose entries fit the project, proposed by a model that has looked at the repository.
An ignore file that already exists is never changed.
A folder that is not under version control is filtered by the same ignore files.
Each stored relationship records whether it was read directly from the source, inferred by resolution, or chosen among several candidates.
The record is returned with the relationship wherever relationships are read.
A relationship stored before this change reads as of unknown origin until its file is next refreshed.
Each indexed repository's code is grouped into subsystems from its stored relationships.
Each subsystem has a summary and a list of its connections to other subsystems.
The analyzer's context for a request includes the summaries of the subsystems the request touches.
Grouping is repeatable: the same graph gives the same groups.
Subsystem summaries are written by the local model.
Files in Rust, C#, C and C++ produce entities and relationships of the same kinds as the languages read today.
SQL files produce entities for the objects they define and relationships for the objects they refer to, where today an SQL file is stored as one whole document.
A language whose reader cannot be loaded on a machine is skipped with a stated reason, and the other languages are unaffected.
The languages the index reads are listed where the user can see them.
Relationships between documents, and between a document and the code it describes, are stored.
A relationship a model proposed is marked as such, apart from one read directly from a link or a reference in the text.
Model-proposed relationships are extracted by the mid-tier model.
Model-proposed relationships are used only when at least 95% of those proposed are right and at least 60% of the real ones are found, on at least 100 hand-checked links.
Only new or changed documents are sent to the model.
The temporary allowance for the MCP server's process to open the live store is removed with this Story.

citations.quotedText: A resolved edge is silently dropped when its target is not stored yet.
The graph store keeps entity rows keyed by a numeric id and has no index by repository or by file.
Accuracy is primary; cost is the least priority.
No direct cloud REST calls from our process.
